cases.name: isJsonValue > checks strict JSON without normalizing it
cases.note: Native half: nested valid JSON round-trips; non-finite numbers unrepresentable and rejected by parse. undefined/Uint8Array/cyclic are unrepresentable in the Rust Value type (embedded-only).

cases.name: copyJson > copies strict JSON without retaining aliases
cases.note: Value containers are Arc copy-on-write, so copy_json shares storage but mutation isolation (the observable contract) holds; JS object identity (not.toBe) is not observable natively.

cases.name: copyJson > optionally omits undefined object properties without normalizing arrays
cases.note: Depends on JS undefined; Rust Value cannot hold it and copy_json has no omitUndefinedProperties option.

cases.name: copyJson > preserves null prototypes and own __proto__ data properties
cases.note: Native half: own __proto__ key is an ordinary data key preserved through parse/copy/stringify. Prototype checks are embedded-only.

cases.name: copyJson > rejects cycles and non-strict container properties
cases.note: Cycles, sparse arrays, extra array props, subclasses, accessors, non-enumerable and symbol keys cannot exist in Rust Value (excluded by construction).

cases.name: tracker ownership > takes immutable ownership of the imported revision in O(1)
cases.note: Tracker::new(Arc) keeps the same Arc and nested container pointers. Object.isFrozen check is embedded-only.

cases.name: tracker ownership > preserves null prototypes in an alias-free owned root
cases.note: Prototype semantics; root identity retention is covered by the O(1) ownership test.

cases.name: tracker ownership > does not traverse a trusted root while taking ownership
cases.note: Accessor-based; Tracker::new is a pointer move with no traversal (see ownership test).

cases.name: tracker ownership > copies assigned and inserted values immediately
cases.note: Splice payload is isolated from later mutation of the caller's value (COW); replica via apply(base, ops) equals prepared value.
